newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH POLLS LIKELY ON SEPTEMBER 14 OR 21.
newsitem.headline: POLISH POLLS LIKELY ON SEPTEMBER 14 OR 21.

text.p: The speaker of Poland's lower house of parliament Jozef Zych said on Thursday he was likely to set the date of this year's parliamentary elections for September 14 or 21, PAP news agency reported.
Zych said during a meeting with students in the southern city of Krakow that the final decision on the date had yet not been taken, PAP said.

By law, the lower house's speaker must set the election date for a day free of work that precedes the end of parliamentary term by four weeks. The decision must be taken four months before the end of the term, which falls for October 14, 1997.

The elections will pit co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) against a rightist bloc led by the Solidarity trade union, now outside parliament, but neither is expected to gain a majority.

Smaller parties, such as co-ruling Peasant Party, centrists Union for Freedom (UW) or right-radical Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP), are likely to hold a balance of power in parliament.
